fact: The swift-spinning eye of the Eagle — rotating so fast it bulges into a flattened, egg-like shape.
bio: Altair (Alpha Aquilae) is a hot white star about 17 light-years away, one of the closest naked-eye stars. It spins near its break-up speed — a full rotation in under eight hours — which flattens it markedly and makes its poles hotter and brighter than its equator. Interferometry has directly imaged this distorted, gravity-darkened surface.
cultural: The name comes from the Arabic 'al-nasr al-ta'ir', the 'flying eagle'. Altair marks one corner of the Summer Triangle with Vega and Deneb, and in Chinese lore it is the cowherd Niulang, separated from the weaver Zhinu (Vega) by the Silver River of the Milky Way.
